# TidyDisk: free, open source disk cleaner for Mac developers

> TidyDisk finds the gigabytes that Xcode DerivedData, simulators, node_modules, Gradle, package-manager caches and AI tools leave on a developer Mac, shows what each item is, and removes only what the user ticks.

Made by RiekApps (https://riekapps.com), an indie app studio. Source code (MIT licence): https://github.com/prateekcode/tidydisk

## Facts
- Free and open source under the MIT licence. Version 2.0, macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon and Intel (universal), notarized by Apple.
- Install: download https://tidydisk.riekapps.com/TidyDisk-2.0.zip, or `brew install --cask prateekcode/tap/tidydisk`.
- Build from source: `git clone https://github.com/prateekcode/tidydisk && cd tidydisk && ./build.sh` (Swift Package Manager, no third-party dependencies).
- Privacy: the app has no account and no ads. It sends nothing unless you switch on anonymous usage statistics in Settings, which are off by default. Scanning and cleaning happen on the Mac.
- Tabs: Overview, Disk, Clean, Large Files, Apps, Projects, AI, Monitor, plus Duplicates and a menu bar item.
- Disk: where the space went by location, as a treemap, by folder and by file type; one pass over about 2 million files takes seconds.
- Clean: Xcode DerivedData and caches, CocoaPods, npm/pnpm/yarn, Gradle, Homebrew, SwiftPM, Docker, simulators and more. A cleaner is shown only when its folder, app or tool exists on the Mac.
- Three risk groups: Safe to clean (one button selects it), Review before cleaning and Handle with care (never selected for you; cleaning them asks once more).
- AI: what Claude, ChatGPT, Ollama, LM Studio, Cursor and other AI tools cost in disk, memory and CPU, with their MCP servers and local ports.
- Monitor: CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, battery, top processes and a speed test.
- Safety: scanning is read-only. Caches and build output are deleted because the tools regenerate them. Files removed from Large Files, Apps, AI and Duplicates go to the Trash. Every action is logged.
- Menu bar: live free space, one-click scan, optional weekly scan with a notification.
- Native SwiftUI app, a 3.6 MB download (not Electron).
